scope_note: This dataset covers GENERAL (typically nationwide-consistent) licensing/permit requirements only. State-specific variations are addressed separately in Layer B. All claims use 'commonly'/'typically' phrasing unless a fact is established federal law. This category includes residential house cleaning, commercial/janitorial cleaning, and related services. A key distinction is drawn between residential-only and commercial-contract cleaning where requirements differ.

federal_requirements.requirement_name: Employer Identification Number (EIN) / Federal Tax ID
federal_requirements.why_needed: An EIN is a federal tax ID number used by the IRS to identify business entities for tax filing purposes. For cleaning service businesses, an EIN is commonly needed to open a business bank account, hire employees, and file business tax returns. Sole proprietors with no employees are not strictly required to obtain one (they can use their SSN), but it is commonly recommended — especially for a cleaning business that plans to hire employees, which is very common in this industry.
federal_requirements.how_commonly_required: Required when the business has employees, operates as a partnership or corporation, or files certain federal tax returns. Free; issued immediately when applied for online. Not a 'license' per se — it is a tax identification number.

federal_requirements.requirement_name: OSHA Hazard Communication Standard (HazCom) compliance — applies if the business has employees
federal_requirements.why_needed: OSHA's Hazard Communication Standard (29 CFR 1910.1200) is a federal regulation that requires employers with hazardous chemicals in the workplace to maintain Safety Data Sheets (SDS) for each hazardous chemical, ensure containers are properly labeled, and train employees on the safe handling of chemicals. Cleaning products commonly contain hazardous chemicals, so this standard is particularly relevant to cleaning service businesses with employees. This is an employer obligation under federal workplace safety law, not a state or local license. It applies to the employer-employee relationship and does not apply to a sole proprietor working alone with no employees.
federal_requirements.issuing_agency: Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), U.S. Department of Labor
federal_requirements.how_commonly_required: Required for any cleaning business that has employees, because cleaning chemicals are hazardous chemicals under the standard. Not applicable to a sole proprietor with no employees. This is a federal compliance obligation, not a license or permit. States with OSHA-approved state plans may have additional or stricter requirements.

federal_requirements.requirement_name: Federal business license — typically none for cleaning services
federal_requirements.why_needed: There is no general federal 'cleaning service' license. The SBA identifies specific business activities that trigger federal licensing (e.g., manufacturing/selling alcohol, firearms, agriculture, aviation, broadcasting, commercial fishing, mining, nuclear energy, maritime transportation). A typical residential or commercial cleaning service does NOT trigger any of these federal license categories.
federal_requirements.issuing_agency: N/A for general cleaning services (varies by regulated activity if applicable)
federal_requirements.how_commonly_required: Not applicable to a typical cleaning service business. Only triggered if the business involves a federally regulated activity, which is atypical for this category.

federal_requirements_summary: There is no general federal 'cleaning service' license. The federal-level obligations for a typical cleaning business are: (1) obtaining an EIN (commonly recommended, required if hiring employees), and (2) complying with OSHA's Hazard Communication Standard if the business has employees who handle cleaning chemicals (maintaining SDS, labeling, and training). Federal business licenses apply only if the business involves a federally regulated activity, which is atypical for cleaning services.

typical_state_requirements.requirement_name: General business license (state and/or local level) — varies by jurisdiction
typical_state_requirements.why_needed: A general business license authorizes a business to operate within a state or local jurisdiction. For cleaning services, a general business license is commonly required by the city or county in which the business operates. Some states also require a state-level business license or registration; others do not have a state-level general business license requirement. The requirement varies by state and locality. Sources consistently note that 'every US state requires some form of business registration' and that 'most require a general business license,' but the specific level (state vs. local) and whether one is needed at all depends on the jurisdiction.
typical_state_requirements.typical_issuing_agency_type: City or county clerk's office / business license office (most common); some states also require state-level registration or licensing through the Secretary of State or Department of Revenue
typical_state_requirements.how_commonly_required: Commonly required at the local (city/county) level. State-level general business license requirements vary — some states require them, others do not. The SBA advises that requirements depend on business activities and location. This is one of the most commonly required permits for cleaning businesses, but the specific issuing authority and requirements vary by jurisdiction.

typical_local_requirements.general_pattern: Most cities and/or counties commonly require a general business license to operate a business within their jurisdiction, including cleaning services. If the cleaning business is operated from a residence (which is common for solo residential cleaners), a home occupation permit may also be required — this is a zoning-related approval confirming that the home-based business will not disrupt the residential character of the neighborhood. Some localities also require zoning approval before issuing a business license. If the business stores cleaning chemicals or equipment at home, local zoning rules may restrict the types or quantities of materials stored. These requirements vary by locality and must be confirmed directly with the local city clerk's office or county government.
typical_local_requirements.typical_issuing_agency_type: City clerk's office, city business license office, or county government (varies by locality)

common_local_permits.why_needed: Authorizes the business to operate within the local jurisdiction. Commonly required by cities and counties for cleaning businesses.

typical_local_requirements.caveat: Local requirements vary significantly by city and county and must be confirmed directly with the local clerk's office or local government. No specific city rules are provided here.
